name: Oholiab
overview: Oholiab was a male craftsman from the tribe of Dan who was divinely appointed by God to assist in the construction of the tabernacle. His skilled workmanship played a crucial role in the building of this sacred structure, as noted in Exodus 31:6. His work contributed to the physical realization of God's dwelling among His people.
namesAndTitles: The name Oholiab means 'tent of [my] father,' reflecting a proper name of Hebrew origin as recorded in Exodus 31:6. This name does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries significance connected to the tabernacle, which was often associated with a tent.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Oholiab was the son of Ahisamach, as stated in Exodus 31:6. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Oholiab holds importance in the biblical narrative as a divinely appointed artisan who contributed to the construction of the tabernacle, the sacred place where God’s presence dwelt among Israel. His craftsmanship was essential in fulfilling God's instructions for the tabernacle, highlighting the value God places on skilled labor in His service. His role illustrates how God equips individuals with specific talents for His purposes.
